$2\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{3}{5}\right )=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{6/5}{1-\frac{9}{2 5}}\right )=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{\frac{6}{5}}{\frac{16}{25}}\right )=\tan ^{-1}\frac{15}{8}$

text: The lines x = ay $-$ 1 = z $-$ 2 and x = 3y $-$ 2 = bz $-$ 2, (ab $\neq$ 0) are coplanar, if :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Lines are $x=ay-1=z-2$

$\therefore$ $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{y-\frac{1}{a}}{\frac{1}{a}}=\frac{z-2}{1}$ .... (i)

and $x=3y-2=bz-2$

$\therefore$ $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{y-\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{1}{3}}=\frac{z-\frac{2}{b}}{\frac{1}{b}}$ .... (ii)

$\therefore$ lines are co-planar

$\therefore$ $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & -\frac{1}{a}+\frac{2}{3} & -2+\frac{2}{b} \\ 1 & \frac{1}{a} & 1 \\ 1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{b} \end{array}\right |=0$

$\therefore$ $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & \frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{a} & \frac{2}{b}-2 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{a}-\frac{1}{3} & 1-\frac{1}{b} \\ 1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{b} \end{array}\right |=0$

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{a}-\frac{1}{ab}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ b = 1 and a $\in$ R $-$ {0}
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

text: If the real part of the complex number $(1-\cos θ+2i\sin θ)^{-1}$ is $\frac{1}{5}$ for $θ\in (0,π)$, then the value of the integral $\int\limits _{0}^{θ}\sin xdx$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$z=\frac{1}{1-\cos θ+2i\sin θ}$

$=\frac{2\sin ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}-2i\sin θ}{(1-\cos θ)^{2}+4\sin ^{2}θ}$

$=\frac{\sin \frac{θ}{2}-2i\cos \frac{θ}{2}}{2\sin \frac{θ}{2}\left (\sin ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}+4\cos ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}\right )}$

$\mathrm{Re}(z)=\frac{1}{2\left (\sin ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}+4\cos ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}\right )}=\frac{1}{5}$

$\sin \frac{2θ}{2}+4\cos ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}=\frac{5}{2}1-\cos ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}+4\cos \frac{θ}{2}=\frac{5}{2}$

$3\cos ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\frac{θ}{2}=nπ\pm \frac{π}{4}$

$θ=2nπ\pm \frac{π}{2}$

$θ\in (0,π)$

$\therefore$ $θ=\frac{π}{2}$

$\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\sin θdθ=[-\cos θ]_{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}$

$=-(0-1)$

$=1$

text: Let A, B and C be three events such that the probability that exactly one of A and B occurs is (1 $-$ k), the probability that exactly one of B and C occurs is (1 $-$ 2k), the probability that exactly one of C and A occurs is (1 $-$ k) and the probability of all A, B and C occur simultaneously is $k^{2}$, where 0 < k < 1. Then the probability that at least one of A, B and C occur is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$P(A–\cap B)+P(A\cap B–)=1-k$

$P(A–\cap C)+P(A\cap C–)=1-2k$

$P(B–\cap C)+P(B\cap C–)=1-k$

$P(A\cap B\cap C)=k^{2}$

$P(A)+P(B)-2P(A\cap B)=1-k$ .....(i)

$P(B)+P(C)-2P(B\cap C)=1-k$ ..... (ii)

$P(C)+P(A)-2P(A\cap C)=1-2k$ ..... (iii)

$(i)+(ii)+(iii)$

$P(A)+P(B)+P(C)-P(A\cap B)-P(B\cap C)-P(C\cap A)=\frac{-4k+3}{2}$

So,

$P(A\cup B\cup C)=\frac{-4k+3}{2}+k^{2}$

$P(A\cup B\cup C)=\frac{2k^{2}-4k+3}{2}$

$=\frac{2(k-1)^{2}+1}{2}$

$P(A\cup B\cup C)>\frac{1}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

$\frac{dy}{dx}=|A|$

$\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{y}{x}+2\sin x+2$

$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{y}{x}=2\sin x+2$

Use in (i)

c = 0

Now, (i) becomes

$xy=x^{2}-2x\cos x+2\sin x$

put $x=π/2$

$\frac{π}{2}y=\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )^{2}-2.\frac{π}{2}\cos \frac{π}{2}+2\sin \frac{π}{2}$

$y(\frac{π}{2})=\frac{π^{2}}{4}+2$

text: Let $g(t)=\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}\cos \left (\frac{π}{4}t+f(x)\right )dx$, where $f(x)=\log _{e}\left (x+\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right ),x\in R$. Then which one of the following is correct?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ $f(x)=\ln \left (x+\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right )$

$\therefore$ $f(x)+f(-x)=\ln \left (\sqrt{x^{2}+1}+x\right )+\ln \left (\sqrt{x^{2}+1}-x\right )$

$\therefore$ $f(x)+f(-x)=0$ .... (i)

$\because$ $g(t)=\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}\cos \left (\frac{π}{4}t+f(x)\right )dx$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\left \{\cos \left (\frac{π}{4}t+f(x)\right )+\cos \left (\frac{π}{4}t+f(-x)\right )\right \}dx$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\left \{\cos \left (\frac{πt}{4}+f(x)\right )+\cos \left (\frac{πt}{4}-f(x)\right )\right \}dx$

$g(t)=2\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\cos \frac{πt}{4}.\cos (f(x))dx$

$\therefore$ $g(1)=\sqrt{2}\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\cos (f(x))dx$ and 

$g(0)=2\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\cos (f(x))dx$

$\therefore$ $\sqrt{2}g(1)=g(0)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

text: Let P be a variable point on the parabola $y=4x^{2}+1$. Then, the locus of the mid-point of the point P and the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point P to the line y = x is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, parabola $y=4x^{2}+1$


[IMG]

Let R(a, b) be mid-point of line joining point P and Q where PQ is perpendicular to line y = x.

Let coordinates of P be P(x, y), Q(q, q) and R(a, b) then,

$a=\frac{x+q}{2}$ and $b=\frac{y+q}{2}$

Now, slope of line y = x is $m_{1} = 1$

Slope of line PQ be

$\frac{b-q}{a-q}=m_{2}$ (say)

$\because$ Line y = x and PQ are perpendicular to each other,

$m_{1} . m_{2} =$ $-$1

$\Rightarrow \frac{b-q}{a-q}=-1\Rightarrow b-q=q-a$

$\Rightarrow q=\frac{b+a}{2}$

$\therefore$ $a=\frac{x+q}{2}=\frac{x+\left (\frac{b+a}{2}\right )}{2}=\frac{2x+b+a}{4}$

$\Rightarrow x=\frac{4a-b-a}{2}=\frac{3a-b}{2}$

and $b=\frac{y+q}{2}=\frac{y+\left (\frac{b+a}{2}\right )}{2}=\frac{2y+b+a}{4}$

$\Rightarrow y=\frac{3b-a}{2}$

Put (x, y) in equation of parabola as P(x, y) is variable point on parabola

$\frac{3b-a}{2}=4\left (\frac{3a-b}{2}\right )^{2}+1$

$\frac{(3b-a)}{2}=(3a-b)^{2}+1$

$\Rightarrow (3b-a)=2(3a-b)^{2}+2$

Replace (a, b) as (x, y) $\Rightarrow$ (3y $-$ x) = 2(3x $-$ $y)^{2} + 2$

or $2(3x-y)^{2}+(x-3y)+2=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

text: Let a curve y = y(x) be given by the solution of the differential equation $\cos \left (\frac{1}{2}\cos ^{-1}(e^{-x})\right )dx=\sqrt{e^{2x}-1}dy$. If it intersects y-axis at y = $-$1, and the intersection point of the curve with x-axis is ($α$, 0), then $e^{α}$ is equal to $__________________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\cos \left (\frac{1}{2}\cos ^{-1}(e^{-x})\right )dx=\sqrt{e^{2x}-1}dy$

Put $\cos ^{-1}(e^{-x})$ $θ$, $θ$ $\in$ [0, $π$]

$\cos θ=e^{-x}\Rightarrow 2\cos ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}-1=e^{-x}$

$\cos \frac{θ}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{e^{-x}+1}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{e^{x}+1}{2c^{x}}}$

$\sqrt{\frac{e^{x}+1}{2c^{x}}}dx=\sqrt{e^{2x}-1}dy$

$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{e^{x}}\sqrt{e^{x}-1}}=\int dy$

Put $e^{x}=t,\frac{dt}{dx}=e^{x}$

$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\int \frac{dx}{e^{x}\sqrt{e^{x}}\sqrt{e^{x}-1}}=\int dy$

$\int \frac{dt}{t\sqrt{t^{2}-t}}=\sqrt{2}y$

Put $t=\frac{1}{z},\frac{dt}{dz}=-\frac{1}{z^{2}}$

$\int \frac{-\frac{dz}{z2}}{\frac{1}{z}\sqrt{\frac{1}{z2}-\frac{1}{z}}}=\sqrt{2y}$

$-\int \frac{dz}{\sqrt{1-z}}=\sqrt{2}y$

$\frac{-2(1-z)^{1/2}}{-1}=\sqrt{2}y+c$

$2\left (1-\frac{1}{t}\right )^{1/2}=\sqrt{2}y+c$

$2(1-e^{-x})^{1/2}=\sqrt{2}y+c⟶^{(0,-1)}\Rightarrow c=\sqrt{2}$

$2(1-e^{-x})^{1/2}=\sqrt{2}(y+1)$, passes through ($α$, 0)

$2(1-e^{-α})^{1/2}=\sqrt{2}$

$\sqrt{1-e^{-α}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow 1-e^{-α}=\frac{1}{2}$

$e^{-α}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow e^{α}=2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

text: For p > 0, a vector $\vec{v}_{2}=2\hat{i}+(p+1)\hat{j}$ is obtained by rotating the vector $\vec{v}_{1}=\sqrt{3}p\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ by an angle $θ$ about origin in counter clockwise direction. If $\tan θ=\frac{\left (α\sqrt{3}-2\right )}{\left (4\sqrt{3}+3\right )}$, then the value of $α$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]
 

$\left |\vec{V_{1}}\right |=\left |\vec{V_{2}}\right |$

$3P^{2}+1=4+(P+1)^{2}$

$2P^{2}-2P-4=0\Rightarrow P^{2}-P-2=0$

$P=2,-1$ (rejected)

$\cos θ=\frac{\vec{V_{1}}.\vec{V_{2}}}{\left |\vec{V_{1}}\right |\left |\vec{V_{2}}\right |}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}P+(P+1)}{\sqrt{(P+1)^{2}+4}\sqrt{3P^{2}+1}}$

$\cos θ=\frac{4\sqrt{3}+3}{\sqrt{13}\sqrt{13}}=\frac{4\sqrt{3}+3}{13}$

$\tan θ=\frac{\sqrt{112-24\sqrt{3}}}{4\sqrt{3}+3}=\frac{6\sqrt{3}-2}{4\sqrt{3}+3}=\frac{α\sqrt{3}-2}{4\sqrt{3}+3}$

$\Rightarrow α=6$

text: If the point on the curve $y^{2} = 6x$, nearest to the point $\left (3,\frac{3}{2}\right )$ is ($α$, $β$), then 2($α$ + $β$) is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $P\equiv \left (\frac{3}{2}t^{2},3t\right )$ is on the curve.

Normal at point P

$tx+y=3t+\frac{3}{2}t^{3}$

Passes through $\left (3,\frac{3}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow 3t+\frac{3}{2}=3t+\frac{3}{2}t^{3}$

$\Rightarrow t^{3}=1\Rightarrow t=1$

$P\equiv \left (\frac{3}{2},3\right )=(α,β)$ 

$2(α+β)=2\left (\frac{3}{2}+3\right )=9$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

text:
Let a function g : [ 0, 4 ] $\to$ R be defined as 

$g(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \max _{0\leq t\leq x}\{t^{3}-6t^{2}+9t-3\}, & 0\leq x\leq 3 \\ 4-x, & 3<x\leq 4 \end{array} \right.$, then the number of points in the interval (0, 4) where g(x) is NOT differentiable, is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=x^{3}-6x^{2}+9x-3$

$f^{'}(x)=3x^{2}-12x+9=3(x-1)(x-3)$

$f(1)=1$, $f(3)=-3$

$g(x)=\left [\begin{array}{ll} f(x) & 0\leq x\leq 1 \\ 1 & 1\leq x\leq 3 \\ 4-x & 3<x\leq 4 \end{array} \right.$

g(x) is continuous

$g^{'}(x)=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 3(x-1)(x-3) & 0\leq x\leq 1 \\ 0 & 1\leq x\leq 3 \\ -1 & 3<x\leq 4 \end{array} \right.$

g(x) is non-differentiable at x = 3
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

text: If $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{αxe^{x}-β\log _{e}(1+x)+γx^{2}e^{-x}}{x\sin ^{2}x}=10,α,β,γ\in R$, then the value of $α$ + $β$ + $γ$ is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{αx\left (1+x+\frac{x2}{2}\right )-β\left (x-\frac{x2}{2}+\frac{x3}{3}\right )+γx^{2}(1-x)}{x^{3}}$

$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{x(α-β)+x^{2}\left (α+\frac{β}{2}+γ\right )+x^{3}\left (\frac{α}{2}-\frac{β}{3}-γ\right )}{x^{3}}=10$

For limit to exist

$α-β=0,α+\frac{β}{2}+γ=0,$ $\frac{α}{2}-\frac{β}{3}-γ=10$ ..... (i)

$β=α,γ=-3\frac{α}{2}$

Put in (i)

$\frac{α}{2}-\frac{α}{3}+\frac{3α}{2}=10$

$\frac{α}{6}+\frac{3α}{2}=10\Rightarrow \frac{α+9α}{6}=10$

$\Rightarrow α=6$

$α$ = 6, $β$ = 6, $γ$ = $-$9

$α$ + $β$ + $γ$ = 3
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift
